At the time of screening, the participant was clinically stable and met eligibility criteria, with blood pressure within acceptable limits and only trace proteinuria noted. On 23 March 2026, she developed significantly elevated blood pressure (155/106 mmHg), representing new onset hypertension and necessitating hospital admission with initiation of pharmacologic management.
The participant remained hospitalized from 23 March 2026 to 25 March 2026 and was discharged on oral antihypertensive therapy. The hospitalization was not reported to the study team at the time it occurred. The event was subsequently identified on 13 April 2026, when the participant presented for a routine obstetric review. An unscheduled study visit was conducted on the same day for clinical assessment and documentation.
Due to the requirement for inpatient hospitalization and the associated potential risk of maternal complications, this episode meets the criteria for classification as a Serious Adverse Event (SAE

On 23 March 2026, she developed significantly elevated blood pressure (155/106 mmHg), representing new onset hypertension and necessitating hospital admission with initiation of pharmacologic management.
The participant remained hospitalized from 23 March 2026 to 25 March 2026 and was discharged on oral antihypertensive therapy. The hospitalization was not reported to the study team at the time it occurred. The event was subsequently identified on 13 April 2026, when the participant presented for a routine obstetric review. An unscheduled study visit was conducted on the same day for clinical assessment and documentation.
